about.title: About
about.heroQuote: A community that seeks God together, shares His love, and lives this truth every day.
about.missionText: Our mission is to proclaim the Gospel of Jesus Christ, fostering spiritual and social transformation through the Word of God. We seek to live and share the love of Christ, forming committed disciples who positively impact the community in which we are rooted.

missionCommitments.title: Proclaim the Gospel

missionCommitments.title: Authentic Fellowship

missionCommitments.title: Mercy & Justice
missionCommitments.description: Serving through concrete acts of compassion, mercy, and justice.

missionCommitments.title: All Generations
missionCommitments.description: Reaching and valuing children, youth, adults, and the elderly.

about.missionClosing: Join us in this mission of bringing hope and the abundant life that only Christ can offer.
about.whoWeAreText: The history of the Reformed Evangelical Church (ERE) La Chapelle in Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort is closely tied to the rich Protestant tradition of the Cévennes, a region marked by centuries of reformed faith and religious resistance.
about.originsText: Born from the desire to maintain a distinct reformed evangelical identity, the community is today established on the Boulevard des Remparts in Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort and affiliated with UNEPREF (National Union of Reformed Evangelical Protestant Churches of France). The responsible pastors are Paulo Sicoli (associate pastor) and Nicolas Thébault (interim pastor).

originsDates.label: First records of the ERE in Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort
Separation of Church and State in France — reorganization of French Protestantism
Inauguration of the current temple on Boulevard des Remparts

about.localContextText: Saint-Hippolyte-du-Fort is known for its rich Protestant heritage. In the 17th century, the town was predominantly Huguenot, with approximately 98% of its population adhering to the Reformed faith. After the revocation of the Edict of Nantes in 1685, the original temple was destroyed and a fort was built to contain the local Protestants. In addition to ERE La Chapelle, the town is home to the Grand Temple, built between 1820 and 1822. It is one of the largest Protestant temples in France, characterized by its neoclassical architecture and impressive organ dating from 1854.
about.communityLifeText: ERE La Chapelle holds services every Sunday at 10am, in French. The church is active in the spiritual and community life of the region, offering times of prayer, worship, and Bible study.
